oneOf.description:
A session's current state for the fleet index; sent for every session after the vault's
hello, then whenever any of it changes. Replaces what the vault had for the session.
Consecutive journal events of one session.
An image a `user_message` of the next batch names; sent just before that batch.

List the secrets in the sets granted to this host, without values; answered with
[`VaultMessage::SecretList`].

request_id.description: Chosen by the host to match the answer.

oneOf.description:
Fetch secrets' values for one of this host's sessions; answered with
[`VaultMessage::SecretValues`], or [`VaultMessage::SecretsRefused`] when any of them
cannot be handed out. The vault records each value it hands out.

Attachment.description: An image or file a prompt carried, kept on the session's host.

media_type.description: One of [`IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES`] for an image; [`FILE_MEDIA_TYPE`] for a file.

name.description: The file's name, as sent; absent for an image.

size.description: Size of the image or file in bytes.

AttachmentData.description: The bytes of an image or file a prompt of a session carried.

attachment.description:
The image or file as the `user_message` names it. The vault refuses it as a bad request
unless `size` is the length of `data` and, for an image, `media_type` is one of
[`crate::IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES`] and `size` at most [`crate::MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`], for a file,
`size` is at most [`crate::MAX_FILE_BYTES`]; or when it holds different bytes under its
id.

AttachmentId.description: Identifies an image a prompt carried, within its session; a ULID string, opaque.

Batch.description: Events of one session with consecutive seqs, oldest first.

events.description: One to [`MAX_BATCH_EVENTS`] events, each seq one more than the one before.

session_id.description: Session whose journal holds the events.

BotId.description: Identifies a chat bot on a host; the name its owner gave it, opaque to receivers.

BotKind.description: The chat a bot is a bot of.

oneOf.description: A Slack app, connected over Socket Mode.

BotPlace.description: Where in a chat a message to a bot was written.

oneOf.description: A direct message with the bot.
A channel or group, or a thread in one.

name.description:
The channel's name, as the chat showed it when the session started, such as
`general`; its id when the chat gave no name.

Bytes.description: Raw bytes, encoded as a standard padded base64 string.

CiStatus.description: Combined status of a pull request's checks.

HostHello.description: Opening message of a host connection.

attachments_cap.description:
Most bytes of this host's images the vault keeps, oldest evicted first to make room
for a new one; absent when the host backs up no images, so the vault keeps none it
sends.

build.description: Build name and version, for logs, e.g. `herder/0.1.0`.

host_id.description: The host; must be the host this connection's device was paired as.

pairing_code.description:
One-time code from the vault's pairing, sent by a host that is not paired yet; ignored
once it is.

HostId.description: Identifies a host running a daemon; a ULID string, opaque to receivers.

HostSecretFetch.description: A host's request for secrets' values for its own use.

purpose.description:
What the values are for, such as `bot:trip1-team`, as the vault's audit records it;
refused unless [`crate::is_valid_secret_purpose`] accepts it.

request_id.description: Chosen by the host to match the answer.

secrets.description:
The secrets, named as a session would name them among the sets granted for host use;
at least one.

JournalRecord.description: One event of a session's journal, exactly as the host stored it.

at.description: When the host recorded the event.

by.description: User whose command caused the event; absent when the agent or the daemon caused it.

seq.description: Position in the session's journal, gap-free from 1.

Mergeable.description: Whether a pull request can merge cleanly.

oneOf.description: GitHub has not computed it yet.

PrState.description: Lifecycle state of a pull request.

ProjectId.description:
Identifies a project across hosts.

From a remote, it is the host and repository path, as in `github.com/org/repo`. For a
repository without one, it is the host id and absolute path, as in
`01J9HOST:/home/dev/scratch`.

PullRequest.description: A GitHub pull request tracked for a session.

head_branch.description:
Branch the pull request merges from, as a short name; absent from events journaled
before herder recorded it.

head_sha.description:
Commit the pull request's branch points at; absent from events journaled before herder
recorded it.

unresolved_threads.description:
Review threads not yet resolved; absent from events journaled before herder recorded
it.

RawEventBody.description: An event body exactly as the host stored it: an `EventBody` of the client protocol (see `server_message.json`), or a type newer than the receiver, kept verbatim.

ReviewStatus.description: Review verdict on a pull request.

SecretFetch.description: A host's request for secrets' values.

request_id.description: Chosen by the host to match the answer.

secrets.description: The secrets, as the session named them; at least one.

session_id.description: The session of this host the values are for, as the vault's audit records it.

SecretRef.description: A secret as a host's session names it: `NAME`, or `set/NAME` when more than one set granted to the host has `NAME`.

SessionId.description: Identifies a session; a ULID string, opaque to receivers.

SessionOrigin.description:
The bot that started a session, and who it started it for where. Set when the session is
created and never changed; a thread linked to a session later does not make it one.

bot_id.description: The bot, on the session's host.

by.description: Who wrote the message that started it, by their allowlist display name.

SessionStatus.description: Where a session stands, as shown in lists.

oneOf.description: The agent is working, or waiting for its primary session to answer an approval or question.

A prompt waits for host capacity or its reported usage reset (retry_at); the turn starts, and the
status becomes `running`, once it does. Survives a daemon restart, and the prompt keeps
its place in the host's queue.
Blocked on a user: an approval or question routed or escalated to the user, or a failed turn to act on.

Its account needs logging in again (`Account.needs_login`): prompts sent meanwhile are
held in the queue instead of starting turns that would fail, and run in order once the
account is logged in again or the session switches to another account.
Put away by a user; read-only.
Handed off to another host; read-only here.

SessionSummary.description: A session as the fleet index lists it.

branch.description:
Branch the session's worktree has checked out, or had when it was removed; absent for
a session that works in its folder itself.

chat.description: Whether the session is a chat, about no project.

head_seq.description: Seq of the session's latest event on the host; the vault is caught up once it holds it.

origin.description: The bot that started the session; absent when the apps or an agent did.

parent.description: Primary session of the task this session is a child of; absent for a top-level session.

parent_host.description:
Host the parent runs on when it lives on another machine; absent when the parent, if
any, is a session of the same host.

project_id.description:
Project of the session's repository, as resolved under the host's current config; for
a chat, the local project id of its folder, which no project has.

prs.description: Every pull request tracked for the session.

repo.description: Absolute path of the repository on the host.

task.description: Short label of the session's task.

title.description: The session's current title; absent until it has one.

UserId.description: Identifies a named user of a daemon; a ULID string, opaque to receivers.
